evidence: In PowerToys 0.98, Quick Access features fail when the icon is selected from notification-area overflow, while the pinned tray icon works; reporter supplied a PowerToys report ZIP and screenshots.
Issue body contrasts the hidden-icon overflow invocation with the working pinned-icon invocation.
Reporter attached a PowerToysReport ZIP and two screenshots.
Current src/runner/tray_icon.cpp routes single click through click_timer_elapsed and open_quick_access_flyout_window; src/runner/quick_access_host.cpp signals the separate Quick Access process.
Inspected src/runner/tray_icon.cpp: WM_LBUTTONUP starts a double-click timer and later single-click callback shows Quick Access.
Inspected src/runner/quick_access_host.cpp: show() starts the host and signals its show event.
No overflow-specific branch or established root cause was evident in these entry points.
The shell overflow may deliver a different notification sequence that leaves tray single/double-click state stale, suppressing or misrouting Quick Access activation.

actions.label: Reproduce tray overflow activation

setup: Pin the PowerToys tray icon for comparison, then hide it in notification-area overflow.
steps: Click the pinned PowerToys icon once and test the Quick Access controls shown.
Open notification-area overflow, click the hidden PowerToys icon once, and test the same controls.
Record whether Quick Access opens, which controls fail, and whether a second click or restarting PowerToys changes the result.
reproduce.expected_result: The same Quick Access surface and controls should work from the pinned and overflow tray icon.
prerequisites: Windows 11 with the PowerToys tray icon visible.
Quick Access enabled; use the reporter-provided diagnostic ZIP and screenshots as context.
reproduce.title: Normalize tray overflow single-click dispatch

verification: Repeat the supplied overflow-versus-pinned comparison and confirm the same Quick Access controls respond on both paths.
Verify double-click still opens Settings and single click opens Quick Access.

proposed_fixes.title: Normalize tray overflow single-click dispatch
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The shell overflow may deliver a different notification sequence that leaves tray single/double-click state stale, suppressing or misrouting Quick Access activation.
plan: Capture and compare notification messages received from pinned and overflow icons.
Normalize single-click state per activation so an overflow click cannot be lost to stale double-click state.
Add a regression test for duplicate or late click notifications and verify the Quick Access host receives one show signal.
